IncidentBot: PAGER: production-inference us-west-2 — sustained error-rate > 8% and 95th latency elevated since 22:01 UTC. Autoscaler activity spike observed. Runbook: <https://rwd.infra/runbooks/autoscale-brownout|autoscale-brownout>

sre-jen: I'm on it, grabbing alerts + timelines. which customers/routes are hitting this?

oncall-tim: i’m paged, joining. i see a big scale up ~21:58 then rapid scale-downs since 22:01. looks like pods repeatedly CrashLoopBackOff on inference-runtime.

eng-runtime-lee: got logs from a few pods — containers logging CUDA OOM followed by kubelet evicting pods. sample:```
E tensorflow/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_driver.cc:368] failed to allocate 3.50GiB (3758096384 bytes) : CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
E inference_runtime] Caught exception: CUDA out of memory
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/serve/runner.py", line 412, in handle_request
    alloc = cudaAllocator.allocate(batch_size*context_size)
```

support-ana: support dashboards show ~14 customers with elevated 5xx on text-generation route `/v1/generate` and embed route `/v1/embeddings` since ~22:00 UTC. SLA impact: degraded for some Dedicated customers (not all).

sre-jen: kubectl output from affected node pool:```
$ kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep inference-runtime
inference-runtime-5f6d8   0/1 CrashLoopBackOff   3 (2m ago)   2d   10.0.5.23   gpu-node-12
inference-runtime-6a7c1   0/1 OOMKilled           1 (1m ago)   2d   10.0.6.11   gpu-node-14
```
and describe shows frequent restarts with `OOMKilled` and `OOM` in container status. autoscaler logs show scaleUp then scaleDown cycles ~every 30s.

oncall-tim: hypothesis: aggressive autoscaler config + unstable node images -> pods start, try to warm kv cache, OOM -> restart -> autoscaler thinks capacity not used -> scales down -> eviction/trash -> more cold starts. churn spirals. we should pause autoscaling and stabilize.

eng-runtime-lee: agreed. mitigation plan: 1) pause autoscaler for us-west-2 (scale controller: set cooldown=600s / suspend scaling) 2) mark problematic node group as `node.kubernetes.io/unschedulable=false`? actually cordon nodes with driver issues and drain gracefully 3) apply temporary lower `threads_per_gpu` / limit batch_size to reduce mem pressure 4) fallback to cpu-quantized model variant for some traffic 5) bump PodDisruptionBudget and add anti-affinity to spread pods.

infra-ellie: taking cordon + drain on nodes with repeated kernel crashes (gpu-node-12/14). i'll capture `dmesg` and GPU driver logs. if driver shows resets we may need a rolling restart of the driver daemonset.

sre-jen: i'll update runbook step and run `kubectl scale --replicas=0 -n autoscaler autoscaler-controller` to pause, and then re-evaluate after drains. toggling scaling now (will post command output).

sre-jen: command output:```
Scaled deployment "autoscaler-controller" to 0
Autoscaling suspended for cluster us-west-2
```

oncall-tim: good. eng-runtime-lee can you push hotfix to reduce default batch to 1 and disable prefetch? small config patch to runtime configmap will be low-risk.

eng-runtime-lee: pushing config change now. patch:```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  batch_size: "1"
  prefetch_enabled: "false"
```
applied. rolling restart scheduled for next 30s.

support-ana: drafting status page update: "We are investigating elevated error rates and latency for inference in us-west-2. Some customers may see 5xx errors or increased latency. Engineers are actively mitigating." dm me immediate impact list and I’ll post.

pm-ben: priority on minimizing customer impact. putting search-autocomplete and critical billing pipelines on traffic-swap to non-affected region as fallback. need IP ranges/route config from infra.

infra-ellie: provided drain started. found repeated GPU driver `GPU reset` in kernel logs which coincides with pod restarts. collecting full logs to open ticket with cloud vendor if driver-level resets continue.

eng-runtime-lee: after patch rollout, early telemetry looks better — fewer OOM traces and restart rate down by ~65% on patched pods. still seeing two nodes flapping.

oncall-tim: i'm taking lead. next actions: 1) continue draining flapping nodes 2) maintain autoscaler suspended 3) monitor error rate + latency for 30m window 4) prepare rollback to cpu-variant for heavy customers if errors persist 5) post status update in 15m. tagging @support-ana to publish.

sre-jen: will run retention of metrics and attach graphs to incident doc. saving logs to s3://rwd-incidents/1729502468/ for postmortem.

support-ana: status update posted to status page and queued customer comms for impacted enterprise orgs.

oncall-tim: handing on-call to @sre-jen for overnight follow-up. i’ll be reachable if nodes start resetting again. thanks team.

eng-runtime-lee: leaving note — root cause probable combination: autoscaler cooldown too aggressive + driver instability under rapid scale churn causing GPU resets -> OOM on cold-starting pods. follow-up: tune autoscaler (increase scaleDown stabilizationWindow, add CPU/GPU utilization smoothing), add node health probe for GPU resets, and add graceful warm-up path for model KV caches to avoid memory spikes on startup.

sre-jen: acknowledged handoff. I'll keep this thread updated and assemble timeline + next-actions for postmortem.

IncidentBot: INCIDENT: severity P1 -> transitioned to mitigation mode. Handoff complete.
